LESSON: READING 14.4.1 FEATURES OF STYLE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.4: Reading 14.4.1 Features of style

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 14.4.1 Features of style. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: where dialogues, similes, and metaphors can be used. Why do we use stylistic devices in writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text
2. use the styles of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in guided context
3. appreciate the importance of style in a work of art

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 14.4.1 FEATURES OF STYLE
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 14.4.1 Features of style helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 14.4.1 FEATURES OF STYLE
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 14.4.1 Features of style”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use the styles of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in guided context

What this means
In this part you learn to use the styles of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in guided context. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the styles of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in guided context.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 14.4.1 Features of style to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the styles of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in guided context. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the importance of style in a work of art

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of style in a work of art. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of style in a work of art.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of style in a work of art. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 14.4.1 Features of style is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 14.4.1 Features of style”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 14.4.1 Features of style to a partner. (skill: use the styles of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in guided context)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the importance of style in a work of art)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 14.4.1 Features of style to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text.
3. Practise this skill: use the styles of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in guided context.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of style in a work of art.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 14.4.1 Features of style from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 14.4.1 Features of style: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 14.4.1 Features of style?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. where dialogues, similes, and metaphors can be used. Why do we use stylistic devices in writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 14.4.1 Features of style means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text.
5. Be able to: use the styles of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in guided context.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
